title: Solo game devs: what tech stack are you using, and would you choose it again?
author: EscapeUA

comments.author: TrickyPlastic
comments.body: I did about 3 weeks with bevy/rust. Avoid it. Compile times will ruin you. Switched to Go.

replies.author: EscapeUA
replies.body: Thanks for the feedback! So, how does it feel?

comments.author: TheAlchimist_
comments.body: Pour ma part C# avec monogame et je compte passer sous Unity pour un gros projet. Actuellement je ne fais que des petits jeux pour apprendre.

comments.author: _CryptoMan
comments.body: The (from my perspective) most important thing is not the technique underneath but more the initial architectural documents, tech specs, and logic foundation of your game including mechanism, skills, story etc BEFORE the implementation with AI starts ;).

replies.author: EscapeUA
replies.body: Thanks for the advice! I totally agree, though I think it’s all about balance. Not everything that looks great on paper works just as well in the actual UI or gameplay. I also think it’s really valuable to get into the feedback loop as early as possible, so you can invest more time in what people actually need rather than in something that seems like a killer feature while you’re designing it.
